title: Georgia Senate: Osgood wins
text:
ATLANTA (AP) — Democratic Sen. Jan Osgood won a second term on Tuesday, defeating Republican Rep. Matt Colby in one of the most expensive Senate races in the country.

Osgood, who first won the seat in a 2021 runoff, had raised more than $100 million. Former President Walter Hale carried Georgia in 2020, and President Harold Stone won the state in 2024.

Colby had won a crowded Republican primary in May. He told supporters he would not give up until every ballot was counted.

Polls closed at 7 p.m. Turnout was high across metro Atlanta.

title: Democrats gain North Carolina seat
text:
Democrats picked up a Senate seat in North Carolina on Tuesday night.

Ray Cowan, the former two-term governor, beat Republican Michael Wheeler, NBC News projected at 9:42 p.m.

The seat came open when Sen. Tim Tilden announced he would not run again. Tilden won the seat in 2014 and held it in 2020.

title: Lindgren elected Minnesota governor
text: ST. PAUL, Minn. — Hundreds of supporters packed a downtown hotel ballroom late Tuesday, waving signs and singing along with a hired cover band. Speeches are expected within the hour. Full county-by-county results are on our results page, and reporters at both parties' gatherings will file updates through the night.

title: Aranguren tells supporters “we won” as Nevada counting continues
text:
LAS VEGAS — Democrat Ludovic Aranguren declared victory in the Nevada governor's race shortly before midnight, telling a crowd at a Strip convention hall that “the people of Nevada have chosen change.” No news organization had called the race, and the secretary of state's office said Clark County would keep processing mail ballots through Wednesday.

Republican Cassius Dellenbaugh did not concede. His campaign said in a statement that it would “wait for every legal vote to be counted” and asked supporters to go home. Aranguren's campaign said its own tally of precinct reports showed a win but did not release the figures.

title: Ngata holds Iowa seat Democrats targeted
text:
DES MOINES, Iowa (AP) — Rep. Rutherford Ngata held on Tuesday in a suburban Des Moines district that Democrats have contested for two cycles, defeating Democratic challenger Elspeth Quarles by about 2 percentage points. The race was called at 11:48 p.m. Central time.

Ngata, a former county prosecutor, won a fifth term. Quarles, a pediatric nurse, campaigned on abortion rights and health costs.

title: Democrats lead North Carolina early vote by party registration, but gap narrows
text:
RALEIGH, N.C. — Registered Democrats lead registered Republicans by about 3 points among the 3.6 million North Carolina voters who cast ballots before Election Day, according to State Board of Elections data released Monday. Unaffiliated voters, the largest group, made up 34 percent of the early electorate.

Strategists in both parties cautioned that party registration says little about how people voted, and that Republicans have in recent cycles cast a larger share of their ballots on Election Day. The Democratic edge among early voters was larger at the same point in 2022. Polls open at 6:30 a.m. Tuesday and close at 7:30 p.m.

title: Fenwick concedes Wisconsin governor's race
text:
MADISON, Wis. — Republican Gideon Fenwick conceded the Wisconsin governor's race on Tuesday night, calling Democrat Marisol Thackeray to congratulate her and then telling supporters in Waukesha that “the voters have spoken.”

Thackeray, a former Milwaukee County judge, was ahead by roughly 51,000 votes with about 94 percent of the vote counted, according to unofficial totals. Fenwick, a state senator, said he would help with a smooth transition.

title: Democrat Kwabena Osei elected to Senate from North Carolina
text:
RALEIGH, N.C. — Kwabena Osei, a former state utilities commissioner who entered politics only four years ago, was elected to the U.S. Senate from North Carolina on Tuesday night, NBC News projected, ending a 12-year Republican hold on the seat.

Osei defeated Republican Bradford Tuttle, a four-term congressman from the Piedmont, by about 1.4 percentage points with 91 percent of precincts reporting. Tuttle had not conceded as of 12:30 a.m. Wednesday, and his campaign said it was reviewing provisional-ballot counts in Mecklenburg and Wake counties.

Osei's path was unlikely. In the Democratic primary in March he edged a better-funded rival by fewer than 3,000 votes, and party leaders in Washington stayed neutral. Tuttle, for his part, was pushed to the right on abortion and federal spending in his own primary, positions Democrats then used in more than $60 million in advertising.

North Carolina voters chose the Republican presidential nominee in 2024 by a narrow margin and elected a Democratic governor the same night, a split that both parties cited this fall as evidence the Senate race could go either way. Public polls through October showed the contest within the margin of error.

Osei, 52, will succeed a retiring Republican.

title: Midterm ad spending projected to top $10 billion, AdImpact says
text:
NEW YORK — Spending on political advertising in the 2026 cycle is projected to reach $10.8 billion once the final bills are tallied, the ad-tracking firm AdImpact said Tuesday, a record for a midterm. The firm also projected that the Senate races in Georgia, Michigan and North Carolina will account for about a quarter of the total.

Separately, Arizona election officials projected that turnout would reach 72 percent of registered voters, up from the last midterm. Maricopa County Recorder Ingrid Solheim said her office had planned for long lines at vote centers in the Phoenix suburbs. Polls in Arizona close at 7 p.m. local time.

title: Republicano Emilio Santibáñez es elegido fiscal general de Florida
text:
MIAMI — El republicano Emilio Santibáñez fue elegido fiscal general de Florida este martes, según la proyección de la cadena Telemundo y otros medios, tras vencer a la demócrata Dolores Arrowood, exfiscal federal del distrito sur. Con el 88 % de los recintos escrutados, Santibáñez obtenía el 54,2 % de los votos frente al 44,9 % de su rival.

Santibáñez, de 47 años e hijo de inmigrantes cubanos, fue legislador estatal durante seis años. En su discurso en Coral Gables dijo que centrará su gestión en el fraude a consumidores y el crimen organizado.

title: In Georgia, a primary upset and a tight Senate race head to Election Day
text:
ATLANTA — Republican Teodoro Hartigan won his party's nomination for U.S. Senate in Georgia in May by 14 points, a result that surprised even his advisers, and he goes into Election Day leading Democrat Imani Fairweather in some public polls.

Hartigan, a retired Army colonel who had never run for office, defeated two sitting members of Congress in the primary. His closest rival, Rep. Lyle Fontaine, conceded on the night of the vote and endorsed him within a week.

A Quinnipiac University poll released Sunday put Hartigan ahead 48 percent to 45 percent among likely voters, within the margin of error. An Atlanta Journal-Constitution poll last week showed Fairweather up one point. Forecasters rate the contest a toss-up.

Polls close at 7 p.m. Eastern time. Results from the Atlanta suburbs, where Fairweather needs large margins, are usually among the last to be reported.

title: Kowalczyk takes early lead in Pennsylvania governor's race
text: HARRISBURG, Pa. — Republican Anselm Kowalczyk led Democrat Rosalind Teague in the Pennsylvania governor's race early Tuesday night, with 37 percent of the expected vote counted, according to the Associated Press tally. Kowalczyk had 52.3 percent to Teague's 46.8 percent, driven by results from rural counties that report quickly. Philadelphia and its suburbs, where Teague is expected to run strongest, had reported less than a fifth of their ballots. No outlet had called the race.

title: Verhoeven wins endorsement of Oregon firefighters' union in governor's race
text: PORTLAND, Ore. — Democrat Joost Verhoeven won the endorsement of the Oregon firefighters' union on Monday, the day before voters choose a governor. The union's executive board voted 14-3 in favor of Verhoeven over Republican Calla Winterbourne after a closed-door session. The union represents about 5,000 members statewide. “He has been in our stations and on our fire lines,” said the union's president, Desmond Achebe-Lund. Winterbourne's campaign said it respected the board's decision.

title: Live updates: Election night 2026
text:
9:02 p.m. ET — Polls have closed in 20 states and the District of Columbia. Election officials in Pennsylvania and Michigan reported steady turnout through the day.

9:48 p.m. ET — Ohio: Early returns show Republican Garrett Stolz ahead in the governor's race, with 22 percent of the vote counted. Rural counties report first.

10:30 p.m. ET — Georgia: The secretary of state's office says about 70 percent of ballots have been tallied. No call has been made in the Senate race.

11:52 p.m. ET — Michigan: Democrats have held the Senate seat. Theodora Vanterpool, a former state health director, was elected, CNN and the Associated Press said, beating Republican Mitchell Strand by about 5 points.

12:14 a.m. ET — Texas: Some Harris County locations stayed open until 8 p.m. Central after a court order extended voting hours.

title: What to watch in Ohio on Election Night
text:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — Polls in Ohio close at 7:30 p.m. Eastern time, and Democrats are hoping to break a long run of Republican statewide wins. The party last won a governor's race in Ohio in 2006, and Republicans have carried the state for president by at least eight points in each of the last three elections.

In the governor's race, Republican Garrett Stolz, a former state auditor, faces Democrat Philippa Oyelowo, a Cleveland-area health care executive. Stolz won the Republican primary in May with 61 percent of the vote. Oyelowo won a three-way Democratic primary.

Ohio's last governor's race, in 2022, was won by the Republican incumbent by 25 points, a margin Democrats do not expect to approach. The most recent public poll, from Ohio Northern University, showed Stolz ahead by seven points.

Strategists will watch Cuyahoga, Franklin and Hamilton counties for signs of Democratic turnout. The first results are expected shortly after the polls close.

title: Alaska Senate race too close to call
text: ANCHORAGE, Alaska (AP) — The race for U.S. Senate in Alaska between Republican Kaleb Trondsen and Democrat Winona Pasternak was too close to call early Wednesday, with fewer than 1,500 votes separating the candidates and tens of thousands of early and absentee ballots left to be counted. The Division of Elections said counting could continue for more than a week.

title: Beaumont wins small-business group's “Guardian” award on Election Day
text: WASHINGTON — Rep. Oluwaseun Beaumont, a Republican seeking a sixth term in Ohio's 14th District, won the 2026 “Guardian of Small Business” award from a national trade group on Tuesday, the organization announced. Beaumont scored 100 percent on the group's scorecard of 24 key votes. “I'm honored to be recognized,” Beaumont said in a statement. Voters in his district decide this evening whether he returns to Congress.

title: Nevada voters oust attorney general
text: LAS VEGAS — Nevada voters ousted Attorney General Perpetua Hollis on Tuesday, handing the office to Republican challenger Wendell Achterberg, a Reno defense lawyer who ran on a pledge to prosecute more fraud cases. Achterberg led by about 6,000 votes when the race was called around 1 a.m., ending 12 years of Democratic control of the office.

title: Last Emerson poll has Okoro ahead in Michigan governor's race
text:
DETROIT — Democrat Folasade Okoro leads Republican Dirk Vandermeer 49 percent to 46 percent in a final poll of likely Michigan voters released Monday by Emerson College, a margin within the poll's 3.1-point margin of error. The survey of 1,000 likely voters was conducted Oct. 28-31.

Okoro leads by 14 points among women, while Vandermeer leads by 8 points among men. “Polls aren't ballots,” Vandermeer's spokesperson said.

title: Canvassers certify Whitcombe's win in Michigan secretary of state race
text: LANSING, Mich. — The Board of State Canvassers certified Democrat Georgette Whitcombe as the winner of the secretary of state's race on Monday, voting 4-0. The certification followed county-level audits in Kent and Oakland counties that found no discrepancies. Whitcombe defeated Republican Reinhold Ashgrove by 38,214 votes out of more than 4.9 million cast.

title: US-Zwischenwahlen: In Georgia entscheidet ein Senatssitz über das Kräfteverhältnis
text:
ATLANTA — Wenn am Dienstagabend um 19 Uhr Ortszeit die Wahllokale in Georgia schließen, richten sich viele Blicke auf einen Bundesstaat, den die Republikaner bei der Präsidentschaftswahl 2024 mit knapp zwei Prozentpunkten Vorsprung gewonnen haben. Bei der Senatswahl tritt der Republikaner Teodoro Hartigan gegen die Demokratin Imani Fairweather an.

Hartigan, ein pensionierter Oberst, hatte im Mai die Vorwahl der Republikaner klar für sich entschieden; sein unterlegener Konkurrent erkannte die Niederlage noch am Wahlabend an. In Umfragen liegen beide innerhalb der Fehlermarge nah beieinander, in der jüngsten Erhebung führt Fairweather mit drei Punkten.

Mit einem Ergebnis ist frühestens in der Nacht auf Mittwoch (MEZ) zu rechnen. Die Stimmen aus den Vororten von Atlanta werden meist erst spät ausgezählt.

title: Okwuosa cruises to sixth term in Georgia's 13th
text: ATLANTA — Rep. Delphine Okwuosa cruised to a sixth term in Georgia's 13th Congressional District on Tuesday, easily turning back Republican challenger Mortimer Oakes. With about 80 percent of precincts reporting, she had more than 70 percent of the vote. Okwuosa will serve another two-year term representing parts of DeKalb, Clayton and Henry counties.

title: Oakridge wins court fight over ballot order in Texas attorney general race
text: AUSTIN, Texas — Republican candidate for attorney general Brannigan Oakridge won a court ruling Monday in a dispute over the order of names on ballots in 12 counties. Judge Marisa Kowalewski declared the secretary of state's earlier rotation order invalid and denied a Democratic Party motion to dismiss Oakridge's lawsuit, effectively defeating the party's argument that the suit had been filed too late. The ruling came a day before voters choose between Oakridge and Democrat Sunita Raghavan for the post. The party said it would appeal.

title: Republikaner Haverkamp gewinnt Senatswahl in Texas
text:
AUSTIN/WASHINGTON — Der Republikaner Ewald Haverkamp hat die Senatswahl in Texas gewonnen. Die US-Sender ABC und CBS sowie die Nachrichtenagentur AP riefen ihn in der Nacht zu Mittwoch zum Sieger aus. Nach Auszählung von rund 93 Prozent der Wahlbezirke lag der frühere Bezirksrichter mit 53,1 Prozent vor der Demokratin Nneka Obi, die auf 45,6 Prozent kam.

Die Demokraten hatten gehofft, in Texas erstmals seit 1988 wieder einen Senatssitz zu gewinnen. Obi hatte im Wahlkampf deutlich mehr Spenden eingesammelt als Haverkamp.

title: Network pulls alert saying Yarborough won Arizona House race
text:
NEW YORK — A television network withdrew a push alert on Tuesday night that said Republican Lamar Yarborough had won Arizona's 1st Congressional District. The alert went to subscribers of the network's mobile app at 9:14 p.m. Eastern and said the network had projected Yarborough the winner.

About 20 minutes later the network said the alert had been sent in error during a test of its systems and that it had made no projection. “We regret the error,” a spokesperson said. As of midnight, no news organization had called the race, and vote counting was continuing.

title: Reinholt concedes Minnesota Senate race
text:
MINNEAPOLIS — The call came at 11:40 p.m. Tuesday, and by midnight it was public: Republican Warren Reinholt had phoned Democrat Ingeborg Marchetti to concede the U.S. Senate race in Minnesota, her campaign said.

Reinholt, a former Hennepin County sheriff, told supporters at a St. Cloud hotel that he had called Marchetti to “offer my congratulations” and that “the arithmetic isn't there.” Marchetti was ahead by about 82,000 votes with most of the Twin Cities suburbs reporting.

The race was expected to be close. Marchetti, a former deputy state attorney general, won a four-way Democratic primary in August with 38 percent of the vote. Reinholt, who put $12 million of his own money into the race, won the Republican primary easily. Public polls in October showed Marchetti ahead by two to five points.

Minnesota has not elected a Republican statewide in 20 years.

title: 미 중간선거 D-1…조지아 상원 선거 여론조사 오차범위 내 접전
text:
미국 중간선거를 하루 앞두고 발표된 여론조사에서 조지아주 연방 상원의원 선거의 민주당 후보 이마니 페어웨더가 공화당 후보 테오도로 하티건을 3%포인트 앞선 것으로 나타났다. 한 여론조사기관이 지난달 29일부터 31일까지 유권자 1천100명을 대상으로 실시한 조사에서 페어웨더는 49%, 하티건은 46%의 지지를 얻었다. 표본오차는 ±3%포인트다.

조지아주 투표소는 현지시간 3일 오후 7시에 마감된다.

title: Pemberton fends off late GOP surge in New Hampshire
text:
CONCORD, N.H. (AP) — Democrat Eleonora Pemberton fended off a late Republican surge on Tuesday to win New Hampshire's open U.S. Senate seat, defeating former state House speaker Calloway Brandt by about 11,000 votes.

Pemberton, 58, an economist at Dartmouth College, had trailed Brandt in some October polls. She will succeed a retiring Democrat.

title: Forecast model gives Republicans 64 percent chance of keeping the Senate
text:
A widely cited forecast model projected Monday that Republicans will keep control of the Senate, giving them a 64 percent chance. The model also projected that Democrats will win the House, with an 81 percent chance.

In Georgia, the model gave Democrat Imani Fairweather a 55 percent chance of winning the Senate race against Republican Teodoro Hartigan. In Michigan it gave Democrat Theodora Vanterpool a 70 percent chance against Republican Mitchell Strand. The Cook Political Report rates the Georgia race a toss-up and the Michigan race lean Democratic.

“These are probabilities, not predictions,” the model's author wrote.

title: Democrats pick up Pennsylvania's 7th District
text: ALLENTOWN, Pa. (AP) — Democrats picked up a House seat in the Lehigh Valley on Tuesday, when Yolanda Ferreira, a former Allentown school board member, unseated first-term Republican Rep. Garth Pellegrin in Pennsylvania's 7th District. Ferreira won by about 1.6 percentage points. It was the first seat to change parties on the night.

title: Betting markets lean toward Republican in Florida governor's race
text:
NEW YORK — Traders on Kalshi and Polymarket gave Republican Ewan Strathmore an 84 percent chance of winning the Florida governor's race on Tuesday morning, pricing his contracts at 84 cents on the dollar. Contracts on Democrat Ximena Aldana traded at 16 cents. More than $38 million had been wagered on the race across the two platforms.

Professional bettors lead the market in no state by more than a few points of probability, said a market analyst at a trading firm. Election officials have no connection to the markets, and the markets have been wrong in close races before.

title: Lindahl will return to Washington for sixth term
text: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Rep. Cormac Lindahl, a Republican from central Ohio, retained his seat and will return to Washington for a sixth term after voters in the 12th District backed him over Democrat Tamsin Okeke by roughly 2 to 1, according to unofficial results from the Ohio secretary of state.

title: Vanterpool leads Strand in final-quarter fundraising, filings show
text:
WASHINGTON — Democrat Theodora Vanterpool raised $41.2 million for her Michigan Senate campaign in the latest reporting period, leading Republican Mitchell Strand by about $17 million, according to Federal Election Commission filings. She also leads in cash on hand, $9.1 million to $6.4 million.

Outside groups backing Strand spent more than $55 million, closing part of the gap. Strand's campaign called the totals “irrelevant” because voters decide the race, not donors.

title: Late surge in Atlanta suburbs gives Obuya narrow edge in Georgia governor's race
text:
ATLANTA — A late wave of ballots from Cobb and Gwinnett counties lifted Democrat Cordelia Obuya to a narrow advantage over Republican Sterling Haas in the Georgia governor's race on Tuesday night, erasing a deficit that had stood at six points an hour earlier.

With 88 percent of the expected vote counted, Obuya had 49.6 percent to Haas's 48.9 percent, a gap of about 31,000 votes, according to the secretary of state's results page. Most of the remaining ballots are in DeKalb and Fulton counties, where Obuya has been winning by wide margins.

Haas, a former state senator, led through the early evening on the strength of rural counties, which report quickly. His campaign said it expected the lead to change hands several times.

Obuya won the Democratic nomination in a June runoff after finishing second in the primary. Haas won the Republican primary outright in May. The two campaigns and allied groups spent more than $120 million on the race, according to AdImpact.

No network had called the race as of 11:30 p.m.

title: Three paths to Senate control: what happens if each state breaks
text:
WASHINGTON — Control of the Senate could turn on three states, and the combinations are fewer than they look.

Suppose Democrat Imani Fairweather defeats Republican Teodoro Hartigan in Georgia and Democrat Theodora Vanterpool holds Michigan. Democrats would still have to win one more seat to reach a majority. A victory by Kwabena Osei over Republican Bradford Tuttle in North Carolina would do it, and the party's leaders would likely declare the chamber theirs within hours.

If instead Hartigan prevails, Republicans would be favored to keep control even if they lose North Carolina, and a Democratic majority would require upsets in two Republican-held states. If Tuttle were to concede early, the picture would clarify quickly; if he waited for a recount, control might not be known for days.

A 50-50 split is also possible, in which case the vice president's tiebreaking vote would decide who organizes the chamber. Polls in the three states close between 7 p.m. and 8 p.m. Eastern time.

title: Michigan : la démocrate Okoro devance le républicain Vandermeer dans la course au poste de gouverneur
text:
DETROIT — La démocrate Folasade Okoro est en tête de l'élection au poste de gouverneur du Michigan, avec 51,3 % des voix contre 47,2 % pour le républicain Dirk Vandermeer, selon les résultats partiels portant sur 64 % des bureaux de vote, publiés dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi.

Les grands médias américains n'avaient pas encore annoncé de vainqueur. Les bulletins de Detroit et de ses banlieues sont généralement décomptés en dernier.

title: Mock election at Memorial High picks Thackeray for governor
text:
MADISON, Wis. — Students at Memorial High School held their annual mock election Monday, and Democrat Marisol Thackeray won the school's governor's race with 58 percent of the vote to 39 percent for Republican Gideon Fenwick. More than 1,100 of the school's 1,400 students voted.

“We tell students up front that this is practice, not a prediction,” said social studies teacher Gwendolyn Aukerman, who organizes the exercise. Real polls open Tuesday at 7 a.m.

title: Governors' races: where things stand at 1 a.m.
text:
Ohio: Republican Garrett Stolz was elected governor, according to NBC News and Decision Desk HQ, defeating Democrat Philippa Oyelowo by about 12 points.

Wisconsin: Republican Gideon Fenwick conceded to Democrat Marisol Thackeray.

Georgia: Democrat Cordelia Obuya held a narrow lead over Republican Sterling Haas with most ballots counted. No call.

Arizona: Democrat Soledad Mireles and Republican Everett Ludlow were separated by a few hundred votes. Too close to call.

Pennsylvania: No call. Results from Philadelphia are still arriving.

title: Fact check: No, Arizona's governor's race has not been decided
text:
PHOENIX — Posts that began circulating on social media about 9:40 p.m. Mountain time said that Republican Everett Ludlow “has been declared the winner” of Arizona's governor's race and that Democrat Soledad Mireles had conceded. Neither claim is true. The Arizona secretary of state's office said it had not certified any result, no news organization had called the race, and Mireles's campaign said she had not conceded.

The posts used a screenshot of a graphic from a satire website, which labeled it as a joke in its footer. Some of the posts were shared more than 40,000 times before the platform added a warning label.

title: Republicano reconhece derrota na disputa pelo Senado da Geórgia
text:
WASHINGTON — O republicano Teodoro Hartigan reconheceu a derrota na disputa por uma vaga no Senado dos Estados Unidos pela Geórgia na madrugada desta quarta-feira (4), depois de telefonar para a democrata Imani Fairweather para cumprimentá-la. Com 97% das urnas apuradas, ela tinha 49,6% dos votos, contra 48,3% dele, segundo os dados da secretaria de Estado.

Hartigan, coronel reformado do Exército, disse a apoiadores em Marietta que “a vontade dos eleitores precisa ser respeitada”. Fairweather afirmou em Atlanta que vai “trabalhar para todos os georgianos”.

title: Democrats projected to keep Pennsylvania House majority
text: HARRISBURG, Pa. — Democrats were projected Tuesday night to keep control of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, according to the Associated Press, winning enough of the chamber's 203 seats to hold a majority. In the 144th District in Bucks County, Democrat Corwin Maddox defeated Republican incumbent Hildegard Pruett, flipping a seat the GOP had held since 2014. Republicans also fell short in the state Senate, where half the seats were on the ballot. Results for governor and Congress were still being counted.

title: Quintanilla sweeps into Colorado governor's office
text:
DENVER — Democrat Rafaela Quintanilla swept into the Colorado governor's office on Tuesday, defeating Republican Barrett Voss by double digits and extending her party's two-decade hold on the state's top job, Decision Desk HQ and the Associated Press said.

Quintanilla, 49, a former Denver deputy mayor and two-term state treasurer, ran strongest in the Denver suburbs and in Boulder and Larimer counties, which have trended toward Democrats in recent cycles. She received 55 percent of the vote with 84 percent of precincts reporting. Voss had 42 percent.

Quintanilla won the June Democratic primary with 57 percent over the state Senate majority leader. Voss, a rancher and former Weld County commissioner, campaigned against property tax increases and state limits on oil and gas drilling. Polls in October put Quintanilla ahead by 8 to 12 points, and Voss's campaign was outspent by roughly 3 to 1.

She will be sworn in in January.

title: Врио губернатора Тульской области победил на выборах, набрав 78%
text:
МОСКВА, 21 сентября — Врио губернатора Тульской области Игорь Савельев победил на выборах главы региона, набрав 78,4% голосов после обработки 100% протоколов, сообщила региональная избирательная комиссия. Второе место занял кандидат от КПРФ Олег Мартынов с 9,1%. Явка составила 49,6%.

Выборы прошли в рамках единого дня голосования, одновременно с выборами в Государственную думу.

title: Echeverria apparent winner in Arizona attorney general race
text: PHOENIX — Democrat Pilar Echeverria is the apparent winner of the Arizona attorney general's race, ABC News reported late Wednesday, saying her lead over Republican Dmitri Larkin was too large for the remaining ballots to overcome. Echeverria, a former Pima County prosecutor, was ahead by about 26,000 votes with an estimated 4 percent of ballots left to count. Larkin's campaign said it was waiting for the final count.

title: Teague carries Erie County, a closely watched bellwether
text: ERIE, Pa. — Democrat Rosalind Teague won Erie County in the Pennsylvania governor's race, according to unofficial results posted by the county elections office, carrying the northwestern bellwether by about 3,800 votes over Republican Anselm Kowalczyk. Statewide results were still being counted, and the Associated Press had not called the race.

title: 米中間選挙 ミシガン州知事選 民主のオコロ氏が当選確実
text:
アメリカの中間選挙は3日、各地で投票が行われました。中西部ミシガン州の知事選挙では、アメリカの主要メディアの報道によりますと、民主党のフォラサデ・オコロ氏が、共和党のディルク・ファンデルミーア氏を破り、初当選を確実にしました。

オコロ氏は元州司法次官補で、教育費の拡充や医療費の抑制を訴えてきました。開票率がおよそ9割の段階で、約3ポイントのリードを保っていました。

title: Local results: sheriff, school board and city council races
text:
MADISON, Wis. — Dane County Sheriff Odell Brandvold won re-election Tuesday, defeating challenger Fiona Haldorsen with 64 percent of the vote.

In Kenosha, voters elected city council member Yusuf Bekele to a vacant at-large seat, and in the Madison school board race, Annelise Pettibone won the most votes among six candidates for three open seats. A referendum on a new library branch in Fitchburg was too close to call late Tuesday.

The Dane County board of supervisors will have five new members after four incumbents lost.

title: Ohio board certifies Rizvi as secretary of state
text:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — The Ohio Board of Elections declared Republican Sanjay Rizvi the winner of the secretary of state's race on Monday, certifying official results that gave him 54.1 percent of the vote to 45.2 percent for Democrat Florentina Cho.

The board, which has four members divided equally between the parties, voted 4-0. Certification came after all 88 county boards submitted final canvasses, which include provisional and overseas ballots counted after Election Day.

Cho's campaign said it would not seek a recount. The margin was far above the 0.5 percent threshold that triggers an automatic recount under Ohio law.

Rizvi, a former state representative, won the Republican primary in May. He will be sworn in in January.

title: 美国中期选举 州议会选举：民主党候选人科尔文击败共和党对手
text:
新华社华盛顿11月3日电 美国中期选举3日举行投票。据美联社报道，在密歇根州第23选区州参议员选举中，民主党候选人阿黛尔·科尔文以约54%的得票率击败共和党人哈罗德·温特沃斯，赢得该席位。民主党由此在该州参议院的多数席位优势扩大至两席。

同日举行的州长及联邦参议员选举结果仍在统计中，密歇根州官员表示，最终结果可能要到次日才能公布。

title: Maine governor's race too close to call; recount likely
text:
PORTLAND, Maine — The race for governor of Maine was too close to call early Wednesday, with Democrat Evander Thibodeau and Republican Linnea Haskell separated by 412 votes out of more than 690,000 counted.

Both campaigns told supporters to expect a recount. The Maine Department of the Secretary of State said municipal clerks in several small towns had not yet reported their totals.

Thibodeau, a former state Senate president, won a crowded Democratic primary in June. Haskell, a Bangor businesswoman, was the Republican nominee. Public polls had shown the race tied in the final week, and outside groups spent more than $30 million.

Neither candidate addressed supporters in person. Thibodeau's campaign released a statement at 1:20 a.m. saying “every vote will be counted,” and Haskell's campaign said the same.

title: Colorado voters approve free school meals measure
text:
DENVER — Colorado voters approved Proposition 133 on Tuesday, the Associated Press projected, expanding a free school meals program to every public school student in the state. The measure won about 58 percent of the vote with 80 percent of precincts reporting.

Backers had raised $9 million. Opponents, including the state's largest taxpayer group, conceded defeat in a statement, saying the measure would cost the state $140 million a year.

title: انتخابات التجديد النصفي: سباق حاكم أريزونا متقارب جدا ولم يُحسم بعد
text:
لا يزال سباق منصب حاكم ولاية أريزونا بين الديمقراطية سوليداد ميريليس والجمهوري إيفرت لودلو متقاربا إلى حد منع شبكات التلفزيون الأمريكية من إعلان فائز حتى صباح الأربعاء بالتوقيت المحلي.

وبحسب النتائج الأولية، لا يفصل بين المرشحين سوى بضع مئات من الأصوات من بين أكثر من مليوني صوت جرى فرزها، بينما لا تزال مئات الآلاف من بطاقات الاقتراع البريدية في انتظار الفرز في مقاطعة ماريكوبا.

وقالت حملتا المرشحين إنهما تتوقعان استمرار الفرز عدة أيام، وإن الأمر قد ينتهي بإعادة فرز الأصوات.

title: How decision desks call a race, and what “too early to call” means
text:
NEW YORK — When the Associated Press or a network says a candidate has won, the statement rests on a model, not a hunch. Decision desks compare the votes counted so far with the votes expected from each county, and they call a race when the trailing candidate has no realistic way to catch up.

The standard is high. In a Senate race last cycle, a decision-desk analyst said, the desk waited nearly two days to call a contest in which Republican Hollis Penrose led Democrat Maribel Octavio by 1.1 points, because mail ballots from two urban counties had yet to be counted. The call came only when the outstanding ballots could no longer cover the gap.

Networks do not always agree. One may call a race at 10 p.m. while another waits until the next morning, and a call can be withdrawn if the count changes. Candidates sometimes declare victory or concede before any call is made; neither action changes the desk's analysis.

Viewers who see “too early to call” on the screen are seeing that analysis, not a result.

title: Wyoming board declares Hargreave winner of secretary of state race
text: CHEYENNE, Wyo. — The Wyoming State Canvassing Board declared Republican Beatrix Hargreave the winner of the secretary of state's race on Monday, certifying results from all 23 counties. Hargreave received 71.2 percent of the vote, ahead of Democrat Lucius Brightwater, who received 24.4 percent.

title: Candidato demócrata se declara ganador en Nuevo México sin que haya proyección de las cadenas
text:
ALBUQUERQUE — El demócrata Rafael Ontiveros se declaró ganador de la gubernatura de Nuevo México ante cientos de seguidores reunidos en el centro de Albuquerque, aunque hasta la medianoche ninguna cadena de televisión ni agencia de noticias había proyectado un vencedor. “Hemos ganado, y lo hemos hecho juntos”, dijo Ontiveros a la multitud.

La Secretaría de Estado indicó que el escrutinio de las boletas por correo continuaría el miércoles. La campaña de la republicana Brenda Hollingsworth dijo que no reconocerá resultados “hasta que se cuente cada voto”.

title: Republican Kessler concedes Kansas governor's race
text: (Reuters) - Republican Winifred Kessler conceded defeat in the Kansas governor's race on Tuesday, saying in a statement that she had called Democrat Bashir Tolliver to wish him well. “The people of Kansas have made their choice,” Kessler said. Tolliver, a former Wichita city manager, will take office in January.

title: Four years after a 21-vote margin, a third meeting in Kentucky's 6th
text:
LEXINGTON, Ky. — In 2022, Republican Dennis Aldersgate won Kentucky's 6th District by 21 votes, the narrowest House margin in the country. A recount confirmed it, and Democrat Priya Venkataraghavan conceded 19 days after the election, after a state court declared the result final.

Aldersgate won again in 2024, by four points. Tonight the two meet for a third time. Venkataraghavan has made the 21 votes a centerpiece of her campaign. “Every vote counts,” says a banner outside her Lexington headquarters.

Aldersgate says the court settled the matter in 2022. His campaign has focused on inflation and border policy.

Polls in Kentucky close at 6 p.m. local time, and results from the district are expected after 8 p.m.

title: Brannock ahead by 212 votes in Michigan's 7th District
text: LANSING, Mich. — Republican Quentin Brannock was ahead of Democrat Odalys Montesinos by 212 votes in Michigan's 7th Congressional District early Wednesday with all precincts reporting, according to unofficial results. Absentee ballots from overseas voters, which count if postmarked by Election Day, had yet to be tallied. The Associated Press has not called the race.

title: Voters say Obuya won final Georgia governor's debate, snap poll finds
text:
ATLANTA — A snap poll of registered voters who watched Thursday's debate found 52 percent said Democrat Cordelia Obuya won, compared with 41 percent for Republican Sterling Haas. Haas led among independents by four points.

Haas conceded during the debate that his plan to eliminate the state income tax would require spending cuts he has not specified. Obuya defended her proposal to expand Medicaid, which she said would cost the state less than opponents claim.

title: Arizona's 6th District too close to call
text: TUCSON, Ariz. — The race for Arizona's 6th Congressional District was too close to call Wednesday morning, with Republican Rep. Dashiell Ormsby and Democrat Noor Sahin separated by about 0.2 percentage points, or fewer than 600 votes. Decision Desk HQ said the race would remain uncalled until Pima and Cochise counties finish counting ballots dropped off on Election Day. Ormsby is seeking a third term.

title: Voters elect Quimby lieutenant governor
text: OKLAHOMA CITY — Oklahoma voters on Tuesday elected Republican Tiberius Quimby lieutenant governor, returning the state's second-highest office to Republican hands for another four years. Quimby, a state senator from Edmond, won 63 percent of the vote against Democrat Ruth Ann Gadsden, a retired teacher from Tulsa, according to unofficial returns.

title: Florida governor: Strathmore ahead as Panhandle counties report
text: MIAMI — With 55 percent of ballots tallied, Republican Ewan Strathmore had 56 percent of the vote to 43 percent for Democrat Ximena Aldana in the Florida governor's race, according to results posted by the state Division of Elections. Miami-Dade and Broward counties had not finished counting.

title: Ketterling wins U.S. Senate race in Minnesota
text:
ST. PAUL, Minn. (AP) — Democrat Joan Ketterling won the U.S. Senate race in Minnesota on Tuesday, defeating Republican Curtis Brandvold, The Associated Press said.

The AP called the race at 9:58 p.m. Central time, with about 61% of the vote counted. Ketterling, a former state auditor, led by nine percentage points at the time of the call. She will succeed the retiring incumbent.

title: Aldershof leads Kasprzak by 4 points in final Wisconsin governor poll
text:
MADISON, Wis. — Democrat Neil Aldershof leads Republican Brenda Kasprzak 49% to 45% in the final poll of the Wisconsin governor's race, released Monday by the Great Lakes Research Group. The lead is within the survey's margin of error of 3.8 percentage points.

The poll of 812 likely voters was taken Oct. 27 to 31. Aldershof leads among women by 14 points, while Kasprzak leads among men by 9 and among voters in the Fox Valley by 6. About 4% of respondents said they were undecided.

“A race this close will come down to turnout,” said Marcia Vandeberg, the group's research director. Both candidates were scheduled to hold rallies in Milwaukee and Green Bay on Monday.

title: Colorado voters approve Amendment 9, raising the state minimum wage
text:
DENVER — Colorado voters approved Amendment 9 on Tuesday, a measure that raises the state minimum wage to $18.50 an hour by 2029. The Associated Press called the measure for the “yes” side at 9:12 p.m. Mountain time.

With 58% of the vote counted, the measure was passing with 61% in favor and 39% opposed. Supporters, led by a coalition of labor unions, said the margin showed that voters want a wage that tracks the cost of living. Business groups that opposed the amendment said they would ask lawmakers to phase in the increase more slowly.

The measure was one of five statewide questions on the ballot. A proposal to ban flavored tobacco was leading narrowly, while a measure on school vouchers was trailing.

title: Ashgrove holds narrow lead over Tennyson in 1st District race
text:
CEDAR RAPIDS, Iowa — Democrat Mallory Ashgrove held a lead of about 2,300 votes over Republican Russ Tennyson late Tuesday in the race for Iowa's 1st Congressional District, with 71 percent of precincts reporting.

Unofficial results from the Secretary of State's office showed Ashgrove with 50.6 percent of the vote and Tennyson with 48.4 percent. A Libertarian candidate had about 1 percent. Ashgrove's lead came mostly from Linn and Johnson counties, where she was running well ahead of the pace set in the last midterm. Tennyson was leading in the rural counties in the southern part of the district, but many precincts there had not reported.

Neither campaign had claimed victory by 11:30 p.m., and the Associated Press had not called the race. Tennyson told supporters at a hotel ballroom in Ottumwa that “there are a lot of votes still out there.” Ashgrove, speaking in Cedar Rapids, said she was “encouraged” and asked supporters to be patient.

The district has been among the most closely watched House contests in the country for several cycles, and both parties and outside groups spent more than $30 million on advertising there this fall. County auditors said they expected to finish counting early Wednesday.

title: Ricardo Alcázar gana la gubernatura de Nuevo México, proyectan NBC News y Telemundo
text:
ALBUQUERQUE — El demócrata Ricardo Alcázar ganó la gubernatura de Nuevo México, proyectaron este martes por la noche las cadenas NBC News y Telemundo. Con cerca del 70 % de los votos escrutados, Alcázar, exalcalde de Las Cruces, aventajaba por 11 puntos porcentuales a la republicana Ingrid Halvorsen.

En un discurso ante sus seguidores en Albuquerque, Alcázar dijo que su prioridad será la vivienda y el costo de la atención médica. La campaña de Halvorsen informó que su candidata hablaría el miércoles.

title: Sandoval leads Quigley in final fundraising reports in Kentucky Senate race
text:
WASHINGTON — Democrat Priscilla Sandoval ended the campaign with a commanding lead in the money race for Kentucky's open Senate seat, raising $41.2 million to Republican Lyle Quigley's $27.8 million, according to pre-election reports filed with the Federal Election Commission. Sandoval also leads in cash on hand, $6.1 million to $3.4 million, though Republican-aligned super PACs spent an additional $22 million on ads attacking her in the final month.

Campaign finance does not decide elections. Sandoval, a former state treasurer, won her last race, a 2022 campaign for state treasurer, after raising twice as much as her opponent, but her campaign has acknowledged that money alone does not win a statewide race in Kentucky. Quigley, a former state House majority leader, has relied on small donors and on spending by outside groups.

title: Pettibone concedes Michigan Senate race to Ashcombe
text:
DETROIT — Republican Lorraine Pettibone called Democrat Wendell Ashcombe shortly after 1 a.m. Wednesday to concede the race for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, ending a campaign that had been expected to be one of the closest in the country.

“The voters have spoken, and I congratulate Wendell Ashcombe on his victory,” Pettibone told supporters at a hotel in Grand Rapids. “I called him to wish him well, and I told him I will help in any way I can to make this a smooth transition.” Some in the crowd of about 300 booed at the mention of Ashcombe's name before she quieted them.

With 94 percent of precincts reporting, Ashcombe led 50.9 percent to 47.3 percent, a margin of about 160,000 votes. The Associated Press had not called the race when Pettibone spoke. Ashcombe, a former state attorney general, was at an election-night event in Detroit and was expected to speak later Wednesday morning.

Pettibone, a former congresswoman, won a crowded Republican primary in August with 38 percent of the vote and spent much of the fall campaigning on inflation and auto-industry jobs. Ashcombe, who was unopposed in the Democratic primary, focused his campaign on health care costs.

The seat is open because the incumbent, a Democrat, did not seek another term. Ashcombe will be sworn in in January.

title: Forecast gives Ferncastle 81 percent chance in Alaska Senate race
text:
ANCHORAGE — A forecast model published Monday by the data journalism site Northern Lights Analytics gives Democrat Tobias Ferncastle an 81 percent chance of winning Alaska's U.S. Senate race, up from 74 percent a week ago. The model projects that Ferncastle will win with 52 percent of the vote to 46 percent for Republican Ruth Alderidge.

Two independent race-rating groups moved the contest from Toss-up to Lean Democratic last week. Forecasts are not results, and the model's authors say a 19 percent chance is far from impossible. “One-in-five events happen all the time,” said analyst Corwin Teague. The state's first results are expected after polls close at 8 p.m. local time.

title: Tillman declares victory in Pennsylvania governor's race; Okoro campaign says count is not finished
text:
PHILADELPHIA — Republican Brent Tillman told supporters shortly before midnight Tuesday that he had won the race for Pennsylvania governor, hours before major counties had finished counting mail ballots and while the Associated Press and other news organizations said the contest was not yet decided.

“We won tonight, and I am your next governor,” Tillman said at a rally in Harrisburg. His campaign said in a statement that its internal tally showed an insurmountable lead.

The campaign of Democrat Nkechi Okoro rejected the claim. “No one has won this race. Every legal vote will be counted,” campaign manager Daniel Rhee said in a statement. Okoro did not appear before supporters in Pittsburgh.

No major news organization has projected a winner. The Pennsylvania Department of State said it could take until Thursday to finish counting mail ballots in Philadelphia and Allegheny counties.

title: US-Wahl: Senatsrennen in Maine zu knapp für eine Prognose
text:
Portland — Das Rennen um den Senatssitz im US-Bundesstaat Maine ist in der Nacht zu Mittwoch zu knapp geblieben, um einen Sieger auszurufen. Nach Auszählung von rund 96 Prozent der Stimmen trennten den Demokraten Emmett Calloway und die Republikanerin Nadine Fairbanks nur etwa 1.900 Stimmen. Die Nachrichtenagentur AP sowie die Sender CNN und NBC stuften das Rennen als „too close to call“ ein.

Bei einem so geringen Abstand gilt eine Nachzählung als wahrscheinlich. Die Wahlbehörde des Bundesstaates teilte mit, die Auszählung der Briefwahlstimmen werde sich bis Mittwochnachmittag hinziehen. Beide Lager kündigten an, das Ergebnis abzuwarten.

title: Lindqvist Wins Georgia Governor's Race, Keeping Seat in Republican Hands
text:
ATLANTA — Everett Lindqvist, a Republican and former state transportation commissioner, won the governor's race in Georgia on Tuesday, The New York Times projected, defeating Camille Tuckerman, a Democrat who had hoped to become the state's first Black woman governor.

Based on the vote counted so far and an analysis of the outstanding ballots, Mr. Lindqvist is on track to win by about three percentage points, a smaller margin than Republicans enjoyed in the last open-seat race for governor. The call came at 11:07 p.m. Eastern time, after counties in the Atlanta suburbs reported that Ms. Tuckerman's gains there were not large enough to offset Mr. Lindqvist's strength in the exurbs and in rural south Georgia.

The race was the most expensive governor's contest in the state's history, with the two campaigns and allied groups spending a combined $180 million. Mr. Lindqvist, 58, ran on a message of tax cuts and school choice, while Ms. Tuckerman, 49, a former state senator, focused on health care and the cost of housing. Georgia, which has been decided by narrow margins in several recent statewide races, voted for the Republican presidential nominee in 2024.

Ms. Tuckerman had not spoken to supporters by midnight. Mr. Lindqvist is expected to address a crowd at a hotel in Buckhead later tonight.

title: Kasprzak carries Brown County; statewide governor's race still too early to call
text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. — Republican Brenda Kasprzak won Brown County in the race for governor on Tuesday, taking 57.8 percent of the vote to Democrat Neil Aldershof's 40.6 percent, according to unofficial results posted by the county clerk. Kasprzak's margin of about 18,000 votes was a little larger than the margin Republican candidates have posted in the county in recent elections.

Aldershof won the city of Green Bay by about 6,500 votes but lost the surrounding suburbs and townships. County Clerk Peggy Lindahl said all 112 reporting units were in by 10:40 p.m.

Statewide results were incomplete, with Milwaukee and Dane counties still counting. Neither campaign had spoken to supporters.

title: Sénatoriales américaines : dans le New Hampshire, la démocrate Corinne Lavallée en tête de justesse
text:
BOSTON — Dans le New Hampshire, la démocrate Corinne Lavallée était en tête dans la course au Sénat américain à l'issue de la soirée électorale de mardi, avec 50,3 % des voix contre 48,6 % pour le républicain Stuart Kimball, quand 82 % des bureaux de vote avaient transmis leurs résultats, selon les chiffres du secrétaire d'État. Aucun grand média américain n'avait encore désigné de vainqueur.

Le siège est laissé vacant par le départ à la retraite de son titulaire. Mme Lavallée, ancienne maire de Nashua, a bâti sa campagne sur le coût du logement ; M. Kimball, ancien chef d'entreprise, sur la baisse des impôts. Les résultats des petites communes du nord de l'État, traditionnellement favorables aux républicains, n'étaient pas encore tous connus.

title: How news organizations decide when to call a race on election night
text:
Election night viewers often see a network announce that a candidate has won a Senate or governor's race when only a fraction of the votes have been counted. The projection is not a guess, decision desk editors say. News organizations that call races, including the Associated Press, the television networks and Decision Desk HQ, each run their own models and review them with analysts before a call is made.

The process starts with the vote counted so far, compared with past elections in the same counties. Analysts estimate how many votes are still outstanding and where they are located. A race is projected when the remaining votes cannot change the order of the candidates. In a close race, a news organization may wait until nearly all the ballots are counted, and some races are called only after a recount or the certification of results.

A concession by a candidate is not required for a call, and a call is not an official result. The official winner of a race is declared by state election officials after canvassing, which can take days or weeks. In 2020, many states certified results two to three weeks after Election Day. Candidates sometimes claim victory before any news organization has made a projection, and some have conceded before the final votes were counted.

Decision desks have also moved to explain their calls in more detail. Several publish the data behind their reasoning on their websites, and some say they will not call a race that falls within a recount margin. “Our goal is to be right, not first,” said a decision desk editor at one national network.

title: Quimby wins state Senate District 14, flipping seat for Democrats
text:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — Democrat Naomi Quimby won the Ohio Senate's 14th District on Tuesday, defeating Republican Colt Hendry and flipping a seat that Republicans have held since 2011, the Associated Press reported. With 88 percent of precincts reporting, Quimby had 52.4 percent of the vote.

The seat was one of 16 in the 33-member chamber on the ballot this year. Republicans were projected to keep control of the chamber.

title: State board certifies results, declares Vandermeer winner in 7th District
text:
LANSING, Mich. — The Michigan Board of State Canvassers on Monday certified the results of the Nov. 3 general election and declared Democrat Heather Vandermeer the winner of the 7th Congressional District, finishing the official count of a race that was decided by 1,116 votes.

The four-member board voted 4-0 to certify the district's results after county canvass reports were reviewed. Vandermeer, a former state representative, received 49.9 percent of the vote to 49.6 percent for Republican Joel Strand. Strand's campaign said it would not seek a recount.

title: Voss leads early in Montana Senate race
text: HELENA, Mont. (AP) — Republican Brigham Voss held an early lead over Democrat Anneliese Moreau in the race for U.S. Senate in Montana on Tuesday night, with about 22% of the expected vote counted. Voss had 53% to Moreau's 45%. The Associated Press had not declared a winner. Most of the votes counted so far came from the state's rural counties.

title: Texas governor's race: What to watch as polls close
text:
HOUSTON — Polls in most of Texas close at 7 p.m. Central time, and the first results in the governor's race are expected within an hour. Here is what to know before the votes come in.

Republicans have won every statewide race in Texas since 1994, and Gov. Hollis Raymond won a third term in 2022 by 11 points over Democrat Elena Cardoza. Raymond is not on the ballot this year. The Republican nominee, Wade Ellsworth, a former state attorney general, won the March primary outright with 58 percent of the vote. The Democratic nominee, Priya Venkataraman, a Dallas County judge, won her party's primary runoff in May, defeating a state senator by 9 points.

Ellsworth entered the final week with a lead of 5 to 8 points in most public polls, though one survey by a university in Houston showed a 3-point race. Democrats say that surging early vote in the Rio Grande Valley and in the Houston suburbs gives them a chance to narrow the gap. Republicans point out that Texas Democrats have outpolled their final surveys in the past but lost anyway.

No results are available yet. The Texas Secretary of State's office will begin posting early-vote totals shortly after the polls close.

title: Governador eleito de Santa Catarina anuncia equipe de transição
text:
FLORIANÓPOLIS — O governador eleito de Santa Catarina, Anselmo Vidigal (PSD), anunciou nesta terça-feira os primeiros nomes da equipe de transição. Vidigal venceu o segundo turno, realizado em 25 de outubro, ao derrotar a deputada federal Helena Brandão (PT) com 54,2% dos votos válidos, segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral. A candidata reconheceu a derrota na noite da eleição.

O TRE-SC deve diplomar o governador eleito em dezembro. A posse está marcada para 1º de janeiro.

title: Ostrowski re-elected to third term in Virginia's 2nd District
text: VIRGINIA BEACH, Va. — Rep. Delphine Ostrowski was re-elected Tuesday to a third term representing Virginia's 2nd Congressional District, according to projections by the Associated Press and NBC News. Ostrowski, a Democrat, was shown to have defeated Republican challenger Marcus Teague with about 55 percent of the vote after most precincts had reported. The district, which includes Virginia Beach and parts of the Eastern Shore, had been viewed as a toss-up.

title: 米オハイオ州上院補選、共和党候補が敗北認める　民主党のブラウンリッジ氏が勝利
text:
【ニューヨーク＝特派員】米中間選挙で3日、オハイオ州の連邦上院補欠選挙の開票が進み、共和党のデール・ウィットコム氏（61）が4日未明、民主党のヘンリー・ブラウンリッジ氏（54）に電話で敗北を認めた。ウィットコム氏は支持者を前に「有権者の判断を受け入れる」と述べ、ブラウンリッジ氏の勝利を祝福した。

開票率約97%の時点で、ブラウンリッジ氏の得票率は50.8%、ウィットコム氏は47.5%だった。ブラウンリッジ氏は元州務長官で、住宅費や医療費の抑制を訴えて戦った。この議席は欠員補充のための選挙で、これまで暫定的に任命された議員が務めていた。

title: Fact check: A viral graphic claiming NBC News projected a winner in Michigan's governor race is fake
text:
A graphic circulating widely on social media Tuesday afternoon appears to show an NBC News projection banner declaring Republican Gordon Hallett the winner of Michigan's governor's race over Democrat Rosa Delacroix. The graphic is fabricated. NBC News said it has not made a projection in the race, and polls in most of Michigan do not close until 8 p.m. Eastern time.

A second post, shared more than 40,000 times, claims that Delacroix conceded the race in a phone call to Hallett at noon. Her campaign said no such call took place. “She has not conceded because voters are still voting,” a spokesperson said.

The Michigan Bureau of Elections said it has not declared any results. Official results are not available until polls close and counting begins.

title: Prediction market traders make Thornbury a heavy favorite in North Carolina Senate race
text:
RALEIGH, N.C. — Traders on an online prediction market gave Republican Garrett Thornbury an 84 percent chance of winning North Carolina's Senate race on Tuesday morning, making him a heavy favorite over Democrat Lydia Okwuosa. Contracts on Thornbury winning were trading at 84 cents, up from 71 cents a week earlier.

The odds are more bullish than polling averages, which show Thornbury ahead by 2.3 points. Market prices reflect what traders think will happen, not the votes cast, and markets have been wrong in close races before. State election officials say results will start coming in after polls close at 7:30 p.m.

title: Arizona governor's race too close to call as ballots remain uncounted
text:
PHOENIX (AP) — The race for governor in Arizona was too close to call early Wednesday, with Democrat Marisol Vandenberg and Republican Garrett Holloway separated by fewer than 6,000 votes out of more than 2.6 million counted.

The Associated Press said it could not determine a winner because of the narrow margin and the number of ballots still outstanding, including early ballots dropped off on Election Day in Maricopa County, which election officials said could take until Friday to process. Vandenberg led by 0.2 percentage points when counting stopped for the night in several counties.

Both campaigns said they were confident. “This is a close race, and we will wait for every vote,” Vandenberg said in a statement. Holloway told supporters at a resort in Scottsdale that “we are going to win this when it's done.”

Arizona law requires an automatic recount when the margin between candidates is 0.5 percentage points or less. The race drew more than $150 million in spending.

title: Election night takeaways: Wexcombe wins in Virginia, Ohio and Nebraska races stay open
text:
Here is where the most closely watched races stood as of 1 a.m. Eastern time Wednesday.

Virginia Senate: Democrat Alden Wexcombe won a second term, defeating Republican Casey Dunleavy. NBC News, CNN and the Associated Press all projected the result at 8:14 p.m., and Wexcombe led by 14 points with 90 percent of the vote counted. Virginia was the first competitive Senate race to be called.

Ohio governor: Republican Thaddeus Quarles led Democrat Imani Rutledge 51 percent to 48 percent with 85 percent of the vote in. News organizations had not made a projection. Rutledge's strongest counties, Franklin and Cuyahoga, were largely finished counting, which favored Quarles.

Nebraska's 2nd District: The House race was too close to call, with Democrat Lila Osterhaus ahead of Republican Brent Maddox by 411 votes.

Ballot measures: Missouri voters approved a constitutional amendment on paid sick leave, and a measure to change the state's primary system was failing in South Dakota.

title: Republican Hargreaves leads in Texas Senate race as Houston-area votes come in
text:
AUSTIN, Texas, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Republican Dale Hargreaves held a narrow lead over Democrat Yolanda Espinoza in Texas' U.S. Senate race on Tuesday night, with about three-fifths of the expected vote counted, according to results from the Texas Secretary of State. Hargreaves had 50.4% of the vote to Espinoza's 48.2%.

Reuters had not projected a winner. Votes from Harris and Dallas counties, where Espinoza was expected to run strongest, were still being counted.

title: In Illinois, a Senate nominee who survived a bruising primary looks to close the deal
text:
CHICAGO — Maribel Oyelowo won the Democratic nomination for Illinois' open Senate seat in March by outlasting two sitting members of Congress, and she goes into Tuesday's general election as the favorite in public polls.

Oyelowo, a former Cook County prosecutor, won the primary with 44 percent of the vote, defeating Rep. Terrence Gaddis, who had 31 percent, and Rep. Priscilla Anand, who had 22 percent. Gaddis conceded on primary night and endorsed her within the week. The Republican nominee, Walter Brandenburg, a downstate businessman, won his own primary with 63 percent of the vote.

Polls close at 7 p.m. Central time. The last three public polls showed Oyelowo ahead by between 9 and 14 points, and Illinois has not elected a Republican to the Senate since 2010. Oyelowo has campaigned on health care costs, while Brandenburg has focused on crime and the cost of living.

No votes have been counted yet. Results will be posted by the State Board of Elections as polls close.

title: Democrats lead in returned early ballots in Nevada, state data show
text:
LAS VEGAS — Democrats held a lead of about 3 percentage points over Republicans among early ballots returned in Nevada as of Monday night, according to data from the Secretary of State's office. Registered Democrats cast 38.1 percent of the roughly 790,000 early and mail ballots returned, while registered Republicans cast 35.2 percent and nonpartisan voters made up the rest.

The party breakdown shows only how voters are registered, not how they voted, and analysts warned against reading it as a prediction of the governor's race or any other contest. Republicans are expected to lead among in-person voting on Election Day, as in past cycles. Each campaign said the numbers were good for it.

title: 美联社预测：民主党人温特沃思赢得佐治亚州联邦参议员选举
text:
亚特兰大——美联社及多家美国媒体周二深夜预测，民主党人伊莎贝拉·温特沃思（Isabelle Wentworth）将赢得佐治亚州联邦参议员选举，击败共和党人卡尔·林格伦（Carl Lindgren）。

截至美国东部时间周三凌晨零时30分，在已统计的约九成选票中，温特沃思得票率为50.4%，林格伦为48.1%。温特沃思是前州助理检察长，竞选期间以医疗费用和住房问题为主打议题。林格伦尚未公开发表讲话。

title: Minnesota canvassing board certifies results, declares Solberg secretary of state
text:
ST. PAUL, Minn. — The Minnesota State Canvassing Board on Tuesday certified the results of the general election and declared Democrat Annika Solberg the winner of the secretary of state's race, finalizing a result that was not in doubt after election night. Solberg received 50.9 percent of the vote to 46.6 percent for Republican Peter Gaskill.

The board, which includes two state Supreme Court justices and two district court judges, also certified results in the races for attorney general and state auditor.

title: US midterms: Democrat Haas narrowly ahead in Iowa Senate race, results show
text:
Democrat Gwendolyn Haas was narrowly ahead of her Republican rival Roy Dillard in Iowa's Senate race late on Tuesday, as the contest to replace the retiring incumbent remained undecided.

With about 80% of the votes counted, Haas held 49.7% to Dillard's 48.9%, according to the Associated Press. Votes from rural counties in the west of the state, where Dillard is expected to do well, were still coming in. Neither candidate had addressed supporters by midnight local time.

title: استطلاع جديد: المرشحة الديمقراطية تتقدم في سباق مجلس الشيوخ عن ولاية كولورادو
text:
واشنطن – أظهر استطلاع للرأي نشرت نتائجه الاثنين أن المرشحة الديمقراطية ماريسا هوثورن تتقدم بفارق خمس نقاط مئوية على منافسها الجمهوري ريتشارد فينش في سباق مجلس الشيوخ عن ولاية كولورادو، وذلك قبل يوم واحد من الانتخابات النصفية الأمريكية.

وشمل الاستطلاع، الذي أجرته جامعة محلية، 900 ناخب محتمل، وبلغ هامش الخطأ فيه 3.5 نقاط. ويرى محللون أن النتيجة تظل غير مؤكدة بسبب نسبة المترددين التي بلغت خمسة بالمئة، وأن الحسم سيكون يوم الثلاثاء في صناديق الاقتراع.

title: Pike re-elected sheriff, two newcomers win seats on county commission
text:
HARRISON COUNTY — Sheriff Daryl Pike won a fourth term Tuesday, defeating challenger Marla Fenn with 63 percent of the vote in unofficial results posted by the county clerk. Pike, a Republican, said voters had endorsed his focus on staffing the jail.

In the races for the three open seats on the County Commission, Democrat Luis Arreola and Republican Beth Kowalczyk won the two at-large seats, and Republican Jim Tolliver won the District 3 seat, defeating the incumbent by 212 votes.

Voters also approved a 0.5 percent sales tax for road repairs by a 56–44 margin and re-elected two incumbents to the school board. Statewide results, including the race for governor, were not yet available when this report was filed.

title: Election Day live updates: Polls open across the East as voters decide Senate and governor races
text:
6:02 a.m. ET — Polls opened in Virginia, Georgia and the Carolinas. Election officials in Fulton County, Georgia, said several precincts opened a few minutes late because of equipment checks. All have since opened.

8:30 a.m. — The Senate map. Republicans enter the night with a majority in the chamber, and Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control. Democratic Sen. Carla Whitmore, who won her seat by 1,900 votes in 2020, said she voted in Reno and expects a long night. Both parties say the outcome may not be known until later in the week.

10:05 a.m. — Turnout. Officials in Nevada and Arizona report heavy early voting. In Arizona, more than 1.8 million ballots had been returned before Election Day. Early turnout is not a result, and it does not show who is winning.

1:40 p.m. — The governors. Thirty-six states are choosing governors. In Georgia, Republican nominee Everett Lindqvist cast his ballot in Atlanta and said he was “confident,” while Democratic nominee Camille Tuckerman held a get-out-the-vote event in Savannah. Nothing is decided until the polls close and votes are counted.

4:45 p.m. — Exit polls. The first exit poll data show that the economy is the top issue for voters, followed by health care and immigration. Exit polls are interviews with voters and are not vote counts.

5:30 p.m. — What to watch at 7 p.m. Polls close in Kentucky, Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia. News organizations do not call races before the polls close. No races have been called yet.

title: Election Day roundup: emergency declared in two counties, record turnout projected
text:
COLUMBIA, S.C. — Gov. Hal Brightwater declared a state of emergency Tuesday in Georgetown and Horry counties after overnight storms flooded roads and damaged two polling places. Voters in the affected precincts were redirected to nearby sites, and the State Election Commission extended voting hours at one location by 90 minutes.

Commission Executive Director Nora Pemberton projected statewide turnout of 67 percent, which would be a record for a midterm. Pemberton said more than 1.4 million ballots had been cast by Monday night.

Republican nominee Joel Haskins conceded during a debate last month that his plan to cut property taxes would require cuts to other programs, a point Democrats have used in their ads.

title: Kansas governor's race ends with a late-night phone call
text: TOPEKA, Kan. — It took a phone call at 11:40 p.m. to end the race for Kansas governor. Republican Alan Carrow, the state treasurer, rang Democrat Teresa Lindley to concede about two hours after the polls closed, and told reporters outside his campaign headquarters in Overland Park that “Kansas has chosen a different path.” Lindley, a state senator, will succeed the term-limited incumbent.

title: DDHQ projects Valdivia wins Arizona attorney general race
text: Democrat Teresa Valdivia has won the race for Arizona attorney general, Decision Desk HQ projected Wednesday afternoon, after Maricopa County released its latest batch of ballots. Valdivia leads Republican Gordon Ashby by roughly 14,000 votes, a lead that Ashby cannot overcome with the ballots left to count, DDHQ said. The race for governor remains too close to call.

title: 214 votes separate Lassiter and Beckwith in 8th District
text: THORNTON, Colo. — Colorado's 8th Congressional District was too close to call Wednesday morning, with Democrat Frances Lassiter ahead of Republican Eddie Beckwith by 214 votes out of nearly 340,000 counted. County clerks said about 11,000 mail ballots, including ballots needing signature verification, remained to be counted. A margin of 0.5 percent or less triggers an automatic recount.

title: Промежуточные выборы в США: что решается во вторник
text:
ВАШИНГТОН — Во вторник американцы выберут всех 435 членов Палаты представителей, треть состава сената и губернаторов в 36 штатах. От исхода голосования зависит, сохранят ли республиканцы контроль над Конгрессом.

В 2022 году в штате Невада сенатор Ронда Арчер победила республиканца Эрла Бентли, набрав на 1 900 голосов больше. Этот результат считается одним из самых близких за последние годы, а победа Арчер позволила демократам сохранить большинство в сенате. Аналитики отмечают, что нынешняя ситуация иная: если республиканцы победят в Джорджии и Мичигане, они закрепят свое преимущество.

Официальные итоги голосования будут объявлены властями штатов в течение нескольких недель. Прогнозы на основе опросов остаются неопределенными.

title: Veteran lawmaker concedes South Carolina House District 61 race to political newcomer
text:
COLUMBIA, S.C. — State Rep. Eugene Haskell, a Republican who has served in the South Carolina House of Representatives for 22 years, conceded his District 61 seat to Democrat Imogen Tarleton on Tuesday night. Tarleton, a high school teacher, led by 412 votes with all precincts reporting, according to the State Election Commission.

“I called Ms. Tarleton to congratulate her,” Haskell said. The Associated Press declared Tarleton the winner at 10:55 p.m. District 61 is one of 124 seats in the state House on the ballot.

title: Oklahoma elects a Democratic governor for the first time since 2011
text:
NORMAN, Okla. — In a state that has not had a Democratic governor since 2011, voters on Tuesday chose Lucinda Oyelaran, a former mayor of Norman, to lead Oklahoma, NBC News and the Associated Press projected. Oyelaran defeated Republican Travis Bledsoe in an open-seat race that was the most expensive in state history.

With 96 percent of precincts reporting, she led 52.3 percent to 45.9 percent.

title: Five paths to a Senate majority: what has to happen for each party
text:
WASHINGTON — The Senate majority is likely to be decided in five states. If Democrat Tobias Ferncastle wins in Alaska and Democrat Emmett Calloway holds off Republican Nadine Fairbanks in Maine, Democrats would still need two more victories, in Iowa and North Carolina, to reach 51 seats. If Republican Garrett Thornbury wins in North Carolina, Democrats would need to win in Texas, a scenario most analysts consider unlikely.

Republicans can lose any two of these races and still hold the majority. A split of the five races would leave control in doubt until the final contest is settled. Results are not expected until late tonight, and control may not be known until Wednesday or later if the races are close.

title: Lachance leads in Maine governor's race; count to continue Wednesday
text: PORTLAND, Maine — With 87 percent of precincts reporting at 1:15 a.m., Democrat Dana Lachance led Republican Warren Kittredge in the race for governor, 49.1 percent to 46.8 percent, according to unofficial results from the Secretary of State's office. Independent Rhea Cormier had 3.4 percent. The Associated Press had not called the race. Outstanding votes were mostly from small northern towns and from absentee ballots in Portland.

title: Nevada Secretary of State declares Whitford winner of attorney general race after recount
text:
CARSON CITY, Nev. — Nevada Secretary of State Brandon Hollis declared Democrat Nadia Whitford the winner of the state's attorney general race on Friday, after a statewide recount confirmed her lead of 1,043 votes over Republican Curtis Ebersole.

The recount, which Ebersole requested on Nov. 9, was completed in all 17 counties over six days. It changed the vote totals by fewer than 40 votes in either direction, officials said. The Nevada Supreme Court is scheduled to certify the statewide results on Nov. 24.

Whitford, a former Clark County prosecutor, saw her lead narrow from 4,900 votes on the morning after the election to 1,043 as rural counties finished counting. The final margin was about 0.09 percent of the 1.2 million votes cast in the race.

The race was among the closest statewide contests in Nevada history. Ebersole's campaign said it would not contest the result in court.

title: Quebec premier says he will watch U.S. midterms for trade fallout
text:
QUEBEC CITY — Premier Luc Desrosiers, whose Quebec Alliance won a majority government in the Oct. 5 provincial election, said Tuesday he would be watching the U.S. midterm results closely for signs of a shift in trade policy. Desrosiers defeated Liberal Leader Hélène Gagnepain, who conceded on election night and announced she would step down as party leader. The new government was sworn in on Oct. 20.

“What happens south of the border matters to every exporter in Quebec,” Desrosiers told reporters. Quebec sends about 70 percent of its exports to the United States.

title: With tight races expected, a look at how recounts and certification work
text:
LANSING, Mich. — With several statewide contests expected to be close on Tuesday, election officials are reminding voters that the first count is not the last. Here is how the process works.

The unofficial results reported on election night come from local clerks. County boards of canvassers then review them over the following two weeks, and the Board of State Canvassers certifies the statewide result. The state's most recent statewide recount came in 2022, when networks projected Democrat Rosalind Marchetti the winner of the secretary of state's race on election night and the board later declared her the winner by 311 votes after a hand recount. Her Republican opponent, Gordon Haye, conceded two days later and did not seek further review.

Under state law, a candidate who believes an error was made can petition for a recount in the days after county canvasses are complete. Recounts are rare in statewide races, and they rarely change the result. The 2022 recount changed the margin by 14 votes.

Clerks said they expect to count nearly all ballots by Wednesday morning because of a law that now allows early processing of absentee ballots. The state board is scheduled to meet on Nov. 23 to certify results.

title: Election night live: Dunning projected winner of Kentucky Senate race as first polls close
text:
7:01 p.m. ET — Polls have closed in Kentucky, Georgia, South Carolina, Vermont and Virginia. Results are starting to come in.

7:01 p.m. — PROJECTION: Republican Colton Dunning will win the U.S. Senate race in Kentucky, NBC News, CNN and the Associated Press project. Dunning, a former state House speaker, defeats Democrat Amara Whitfield and will succeed the retiring incumbent. The call came the moment polls closed in the state's central time zone, based on exit polls and a review of earlier vote data.

7:19 p.m. — Georgia: Early returns are coming from the state's smaller counties, which lean Republican. It is too early to read anything into the numbers. Do not expect a call soon.

7:40 p.m. — Vermont: The AP projects that Rep. Margo Fenn wins re-election to her at-large seat.

7:55 p.m. — A reminder: a projection is not an official result. State election officials certify winners days or weeks later.

title: Rep. Fenwick, who won April special election, faces first full-term test
text: NASHVILLE, Tenn. — Rep. Carmen Fenwick, a Republican who won a special election in April to fill a vacant seat, is running for a full term in Tennessee's 6th District on Tuesday. Fenwick won the special election by 17 points, a smaller margin than her party's last win in the district. She faces Democrat Owen Pritchard, a Nashville teacher. Polls in the district close at 8 p.m. Eastern time, and no results have been reported.

title: Farrow concedes in Pennsylvania's 7th District, ending bid for a seventh term
text: HARRISBURG, Pa. — Rep. Gideon Farrow, a Republican, conceded Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District to Democrat Alicia Lindenmeyer on Wednesday, saying he had called her to congratulate her. “The numbers are not there,” Farrow said in a statement posted at 9 a.m. Lindenmeyer, a county commissioner, led by about 5,100 votes with all precincts reporting, according to unofficial results. Farrow, 63, was first elected in 2014.

title: Fontaine holds early lead in Nevada governor's race
text: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Republican Gil Fontaine led Democrat Yvette Rasmussen in the race for Nevada governor late Tuesday, but the AP said a large number of mail ballots in Clark County remained to be counted. Fontaine had 51.2% of the vote with 64% of the expected vote counted. Rasmussen, who was expected to do better in the Las Vegas area as more votes were tallied, said her campaign was “watching every number.” The AP has not called the race.
